newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: Singapore shares end firmer, red chips steal show.
newsitem.headline: Singapore shares end firmer, red chips steal show.

text.p: Singapore stocks clawed their way back into positive territory on Monday, fuelled by healthy demand for China-linked issues on the eve of Hong Kong's handover.
"Red chips were driven higher by the Hong Kong factor. There was nothing spectacular on heavyweights," a dealer said.
Selected demand for local blue chips like banks and property counters also paved the way for a recovery in the index.
The Straits Times Industrials Index (STII) closed 13.58 points higher at 1,987.95. Gainers outperformed losers by 170 to 152 and volume was a moderate 126 million contracts.
Euphoria for China-linked issues did not appear dampened by the closure of the Hong Kong stock exchange until Thursday.
Newly-listed Tianjin Zhongxin Pharmaceutical ended at US$1.15, up 12 cents on the day but down from an intraday high of US$1.19.
China North Industrial also rose to a high of US$0.65, before settling at US$0.605, up 3.5 cents.
Top gainers were City Development, which rose Singapore 40 cents to S$14, OCBC foreign, up 30 cents to S$14.80 and DBS Bank foreign, up 30 cents to S$18.
Metro Holdings, rose S$0.16 to S$4.68, supported by better-than-expected full year results last Friday.
